### Observed differences

- Four activities became effectively mandatory. In the earlier window A22 appeared in about 54 in 100 traces and A31, A32 and A37 in about 46 in 100 traces each; in the later window A22 appears in all 200 traces and each of A31, A32, A37 in about 199 of 200, exactly once per trace in both windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- The choice point at A21 disappeared. Earlier, about 54 in 100 of A21's outgoing transitions led to A22 and the remainder led into A31, A32 or A37 (about 14–17 in 100 each); in the later window every observed transition from A21 leads to A22. [DIR002]
- The group A31/A32/A37 now sits between A20 and A23. Earlier, A20 always passed directly to A23 (100 in 100 outgoing transitions, one step away); in the later window A20 leads to A31, A32 or A37 in roughly equal shares (about 32–36 in 100 each) and almost never directly to A23 (about 1 in 200), and the A20-to-A23 distance moved from one step in all traces to four steps in about 99.5 in 100 traces. [DIR001, LAG001]
- Order relations around the group reversed. Earlier, A21 and A23 each preceded the group in every co-occurrence, and A22 never shared a trace with any of A31, A32, A37 (strict alternatives, co-occurrence 0); in the later window the group precedes A21 and A23 in about 99.5 in 100 traces and co-occurs with A22 in about 99.5 in 100 traces, always before it. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- The group now hands over to A23 instead of A26. Earlier, each of A31, A32, A37 led to A26 in about 29–36 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and never to A23; later, each leads to A23 in about 31–37 in 100 and A26 is no longer observed as their direct successor, while A26 is reached only after A22 (the A21-to-A26 distance is always two steps, where earlier it was two steps in about 54 in 100 traces and four steps in the rest). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG002, REL010]
- The internal order of A31, A32 and A37 shows no fixed sequence in either window — each pair occurs in both orders in near-equal shares — while their mutual co-occurrence rose from about 46 to about 99.5 in 100 traces. [REL020, REL021, REL022]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the three-activity group A31, A32, A37 was repositioned to run between A20 and A23, and that the branch after A21 was collapsed: earlier, a case ran either A22 after A21 (about 54 in 100 cases) or the group A31/A32/A37 after A21 (about 46 in 100 cases), both closing into A26; in the later window essentially every case runs A20, then the group in an unfixed internal order, then A23, A21, A22 and A26, with A22 and the group activities changed from optional, mutually exclusive alternatives into mandatory steps. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, REL011, REL012, REL013, LAG001, LAG002]

This is shown directly by relational and positional evidence rather than by frequency shifts alone: the successor profiles of A20 and A21 changed, the order relations flipped from "A21/A23 before the group" to "group before A21/A23", the strict exclusivity between A22 and the group became universal co-occurrence, and the step-distance changes (A20-to-A23 from one to four steps; A21-to-A26 fixed at two) match this placement. The 33 qualified items are roughly 70 times the 0.45 expected by chance for the 91 tested control-flow units, and the new orderings appear in about 99.5 in 100 later traces while the reverse order appears in about 92 earlier co-occurrence records without a single exception, which simple sampling variation cannot explain. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]

Limitations: the indicators use event positions and relative order, so the evidence shows the group now lies between A20 and A23 but cannot distinguish the group moving earlier from A23/A21/A22 moving later in absolute terms, and it says nothing about clock-time behaviour; it also cannot fully rule out that the later pattern existed as a rare, unsampled variant before the cut-off, since each window is a finite sample of 200 traces. [REL014, REL015, REL016, LAG001]
